I've written the seam. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors, and the existing suite still passes (326 of 326 tests). Only three of the four files changed; `src/analysis.ts` has no edits, for the reason in the first point below.

**Changes:**
- **`src/sandbox/project.ts`**: adds `NODE_GLOBAL_DECLARATIONS` with all 81 entries from the spec, written out in order and not frozen. `ambientDeclarations` now takes a third parameter, `installed: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set()`, and its body is unchanged.
- **`src/sandbox/provenance.ts`**: adds `isRegistryVersion(version: string): boolean`, whose body just throws `"not implemented"`. Its doc comment says it never throws, because the spec says bad input returns false.
- **`src/slice/manifest.ts`**: `CompilationResult` gains the two optional fields `untypedPackageErrors` and `typedPackages`, with the spec's doc comments.

**Where I departed from your instructions:**
1. **The version constants are not bumped.** The spec says `SLICE_TOOL_VERSION` becomes `"slice@4"` and `SANDBOX_BUILD_RUN_VERSION` becomes `"sandbox_build@9"`. But `test/slice.test.ts:589` asserts `toolVersionOf("slice") === "slice@3"`, so bumping it would break the existing suite. You also asked me to leave existing exports unchanged, so both constants keep their old values. The implementer has to bump both and update that line in the existing test; until then, the new suites' version checks will fail.
2. **Two parameters start with an underscore.** The shared compiler settings turn on `noUnusedParameters`, and their own guidance is to prefix a parameter that must stay in a signature with `_`. So the stubs use `_installed` and `_version` instead of the spec's `installed` and `version`. This doesn't affect callers, since both are passed by position.

Nothing else was touched; `spec.md` is still untracked as before.

Added: `NODE_GLOBAL_DECLARATIONS`, `isRegistryVersion`, `CompilationResult.untypedPackageErrors`, `CompilationResult.typedPackages`, `ambientDeclarations`'s `installed` parameter.

The test suite is written: four files under `packages/core/test/`. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors. When run, 17 of the 50 tests pass and 33 fail. I checked a sample of the failures, and they fail on the behaviour the spec changes, not because of a broken fixture.

Some tests pass because several bodies are not stubs. Only `isRegistryVersion` throws `not implemented`. The others still have their old code: `ambientDeclarations` (which accepts `installed` but ignores it), `generateProject`, `renderBoundaryMarkdown`, `resolveScope` and the version constants. So tests that check behaviour the spec leaves unchanged already pass:
- the empty-`installed` equality (`[boundary-3]`)
- the stub that's not in `outbound` getting `export {};` (`[boundary-10]`)
- absent or empty fields rendering as before (`[boundary-13]`)
- the plain registry pin being approved (`[happy-10]`)
- the type-level `CompilationResult` checks (`[happy-11]`, `[happy-12]`)
- `[boundary-8]`, which compares two outputs that the old code also ignores `installed` in, so they match trivially

**Files:**
- **`workspace-stubs-confirmed.ambient.test.ts`**: tool versions, `NODE_GLOBAL_DECLARATIONS`, and `ambientDeclarations` (`[happy-1]` to `[happy-5]`, `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-7]`). The expected header and the 81 entries are written out from the spec text, so they don't depend on the export they test.
- **`workspace-stubs-confirmed.project.test.ts`**: `generateProject`'s ambient file, package.json dependencies and mock runtimes (`[happy-6]`, `[happy-7]`, `[boundary-8]` to `[boundary-10]`).
- **`workspace-stubs-confirmed.scope.test.ts`**: `isRegistryVersion` and `resolveScope` (`[happy-8]` to `[happy-10]`, `[unhappy-1]`, `[unhappy-2]`, `[boundary-11]`).
- **`workspace-stubs-confirmed.compilation.test.ts`**: the new `CompilationResult` fields and the Compilation section of the boundary markdown (`[happy-11]` to `[happy-13]`, `[boundary-12]` to `[boundary-14]`).

**How the tests are built:**
- **Scenarios with several example rows:** each is one test that loops over its rows. Every happy and unhappy scenario has a second test for an edge case, for example sort order by UTF-16 code unit, a scoped alias, the singular "1 more error", and a uncounted error when no compilation was attempted.
- **Fixtures:** each file defines its own, adapted from `sandbox.test.ts` and `slice.test.ts`, because those files can't be imported without also running their tests. Nothing uses a clock, the filesystem, the network or randomness.
- **Type check:** `[happy-12]` uses one `@ts-expect-error` to check that a `typedPackages` entry without a `version` does not type-check.

50 tests, in 4 files.
